Then the right-hand side of the equation can be transformed into: $$ g(t)=\frac{6 t}{t^{2}+1} $$ The function $g(t)$ is negative for negative values of the argument, and for positive values, it can be represented as: $$ g(t)=\frac{6}{t+\frac{1}{t}} $$ from which it is clear that the function takes its maximum value when the denominator is positive and minimal.
